module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Determinantal conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinantal_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

/- Formalisation note: Here, we represent the two normal matrices as $U_1 D_1 U_1^*$ and
$U_2 D_2 U_2^*$ respectively, where $U_1, U_2$ are unitary and $D_1, D_2$
are diagonal. This is an universal form of a normal matrix,
allowing to retrieve $\lambda (A)_i$ as ${D_1}_{i,i}$, whereas the current mathlib
doesn't support obtaining the vector of eigenvalues from a general normal
non-Hermitian matrix. -/

namespace DeterminantalConjecture

/--
Does the determinant of the sum $A + B$ of two $n \times n$ normal
complex matrices $A$ and $B$ always lie in the convex hull
of the $n!$ points $\prod\_i (\lambda(A)\_i + \lambda(B)\_{\sigma(i)})$?
Here the numbers $\lambda(A)\_i$ and $\lambda(B)\_i$ are
the eigenvalues of $A$ and $B$, and $\sigma$ is an element of the symmetric
group $S\_n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem determinantal_conjecture
    (n : Type) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (d1 d2 : n → ℂ) (U1 U2 : unitary (Matrix n n ℂ)) :
    (U1 * Matrix.diagonal d1 * star U1 + U2 * Matrix.diagonal d2 * star U2).det
      ∈ convexHull ℝ { ∏ i, (d1 i + d2 (σ i)) | σ : Equiv.Perm n } := by
  sorry

end DeterminantalConjecture

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over two normal complex matrices and their eigenvalue lists. Lean instead quantifies over arbitrary complex diagonal vectors and two independent unitary matrices, representing each normal matrix as U * diagonal d * star U. It also permits empty finite index types.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The finite-dimensional complex spectral theorem says that a matrix is normal exactly when it has this unitary-diagonal form. Its diagonal entries are precisely its eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicity. Thus the parametrization covers all pairs of normal matrices, without requiring simultaneous diagonalization or commutation. Reordering either eigenvalue list only reindexes the permutation products, leaving their convex hull unchanged. Any finite index type can be relabelled by Fin of its cardinality. The additional zero-dimensional case is true: the determinant and empty products are 1, so the assertion is 1 ∈ convexHull ℝ {1}.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_matrix (spectral-theorem characterization and identification of the diagonal entries as eigenvalues)

Kijti Rodtes, A class of normal dilation matrices affirming the Marcus-de Oliveira conjecture, arXiv:2006.14846 (2020), introduction, special cases, and direct-sum lemma. LaTeX source read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/2006.14846

review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration. Matrix star/coercions, unitary membership, permutation indexing, and the real convex hull have the intended meanings. Scratch proofs in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify normality of the represented matrices, the characteristic-polynomial formula preserving eigenvalue multiplicities, and the empty-dimensional, one-dimensional, zero-vector, and jointly diagonal cases. /workspace/review/two_by_two.lean verifies an exact non-diagonal unitary example with convex weights 9/25 and 16/25. These checks do not invoke the conjecture; the full spectral-theorem equivalence was not proved in Lean. No conflict with the research-open tag was found in the consulted sources. The original journal links were inaccessible, but Wikipedia's explicit statement was corroborated by Rodtes's paper.
